### ORG-040 implementation result

ORG-040 adds a permanent architecture/integrity guardrail rather than another schema
or production-model change.

The test explicitly protects the known Organization translatable attributes:

```text
AdministrativeState.name*
AdministrativeDistrict.name*
AdministrativeLocality.name*
OrganizationUnit.name*
OrganizationUnitType.name*
OrganizationUnitType.description*
Position.title*
Position.description*
Shift.name*
```

For each domain model the guardrail requires the complete Java triplet
`Ar/Fr/En`. For each corresponding JPA entity it additionally requires the matching
database columns `*_ar`, `*_fr`, and `*_en`.

The existing OrganizationUnit create/query/API chain is also checked end-to-end for
`nameAr/nameFr/nameEn` on:

```text
CreateOrganizationUnitRequest
CreateOrganizationUnitCommand
OrganizationUnitSummaryDto
OrganizationUnitResponse
OrganizationAdministrationQueryUseCase.OrganizationUnitView
```

The architecture scan rejects any future Organization production class whose name
contains `Translation` and any Organization production JPA/runtime source mapping
`hidra_org_unit_type_translation`.

Migration-history compatibility is preserved: historical migrations may still contain
the retired table because Flyway history is immutable. The guardrail instead requires
the ORG-039 retirement migration to contain the drop and rejects any migration ordered
after `V20260927_003__retire_organization_unit_type_translation_table.sql` that
references the retired table.

Employee `*Ar/*Lt` proper-name/transliteration fields, address lines, delegation
reasons, responsibility descriptions, hierarchy snapshot descriptions, and other
transactional/free-form text remain intentionally outside this fixed multilingual
catalog guardrail.

After ORG-040 passes its compile/test/clean-verify and CI gates, the Organization
multilingual correction sequence ORG-034 through ORG-040 is complete and normal
roadmap execution may resume from the previously in-progress ORG-027 work.

~~~~~~~~

~~~~~~~~text
### ORG-042 implementation result

ORG-042 replaces arbitrary ReportingLine source/target discriminator strings with a
closed Organization-owned subject contract:

```text
ReportingSubjectType
  EMPLOYEE
  POSITION
  ORGANIZATION_UNIT

ReportingSubjectReference
  type
  targetId
```

`ReportingLine` now stores typed `source` and `target` references. The existing
database columns `source_type/source_id` and `target_type/target_id` are preserved;
the JPA entity maps the type columns with `EnumType.STRING`, so accepted persisted
values remain the same enum names.

No identity or topology subject type is introduced. Repository evidence describes
ReportingLine as a relation between positions, units, or employees, and ORG-042 keeps
that boundary exact. Deprecated textual constructors/accessors remain only to avoid a
hard compatibility break while callers migrate.

No Flyway migration is added in ORG-042. Existing-data discriminator preflight and
database CHECK/FK enforcement belong to ORG-046. Consequently, any historical row with
a discriminator outside EMPLOYEE/POSITION/ORGANIZATION_UNIT remains a deployment data
quality risk until that preflight is executed.

Focused domain tests reject unsupported/blank textual discriminators and normalize
target IDs. Persistence-mapper tests prove typed domain references round-trip through
the existing VARCHAR representation without adding cross-module ownership.

~~~~~~~~

~~~~~~~~text
### ORG-043 implementation result

ORG-043 replaces the arbitrary `OrganizationContactPoint.targetType/targetId` pair
with an Organization-owned typed reference:

```text
ContactPointTargetType
  EMPLOYEE
  ORGANIZATION_UNIT

ContactPointTargetReference
  type
  targetId
```

The closed set intentionally excludes Position, Identity, Topology, Party, and other
bounded-context targets. Contact points remain Organization-owned operational contact
data rather than a generic cross-module reference mechanism.

`OrganizationContactPoint` now stores a canonical typed `target`. The existing
database `target_type` and `target_id` columns remain unchanged; JPA maps
`target_type` with `EnumType.STRING`, preserving the accepted EMPLOYEE and
ORGANIZATION_UNIT textual representation. Deprecated textual constructor/accessors
remain only for compatibility.

Because the module currently has no inbound contact-point write use case or REST
endpoint, ORG-043 does not invent one. Instead it adds
`OrganizationContactPointTargetValidator`, an application-layer prerequisite that
verifies target existence through the existing EmployeeRepositoryPort and
OrganizationUnitRepositoryPort. It validates existence only; no undocumented employee
or unit lifecycle rule is invented.

No Flyway migration is added in ORG-043. Existing-data target-type preflight and
database CHECK/FK enforcement belong to ORG-046. Any historical contact-point row with
an unsupported target_type therefore remains a deployment data-quality risk until that
migration preflight is executed.

Focused domain tests verify the closed target set and ID normalization; application
tests verify repository-specific existence checks; persistence tests prove typed
round-trip through the current VARCHAR representation.

~~~~~~~~

### ORG-044 implementation result

ORG-044 makes the existing `OperationalScopeReference` value object the canonical
registration input from application command through owner validation and registry
persistence:

```text
RegisterOperationalScopeCommand
        |
        v
OperationalScopeReference
  type
  targetId
        |
        v
OperationalScopeRegistrationValidator
        |
        v
OperationalScopeRegistryRepositoryPort.register(reference)
        |
        v
OperationalScope
  id          <- generated registry identity
  type
  targetId
```

The correction removes duplicate local scope-shape validation from the command,
validator, and JPA adapter. `OperationalScopeReference` remains responsible for
GLOBAL/entity-backed/CUSTOM shape rules; the application validator remains responsible
for owner resolver support, exact identity, existence, and assignability.

The registry adapter now receives the validated reference as one value. It still
persists the same columns and returns an `OperationalScope` with a positive,
database-generated `id`. Responsibility assignments remain keyed by that generated
scope ID; they do not persist an owner-native target ID as responsibility identity.

Deprecated split `type/targetId` command, validator, and repository bridges remain
only for compatibility with existing callers/anonymous repository implementations.
New code is expected to use `OperationalScopeReference` directly.

No Flyway migration, schema change, REST endpoint, topology import, or responsibility
storage change is part of ORG-044.

Focused tests prove that the canonical reference survives command/validation into the
repository unchanged, GLOBAL bypasses external owner lookup, rejected owners never
reach persistence, and the returned registry ID remains independent of the owner target
identifier.

~~~~~~~~

**Pinned original bounded record — historical applicability:**

~~~~~~~~text
### ORG-045 implementation result

Repository review found that `OrganizationCode` was a genuine orphan value object even
though seven Organization reference/master models already expose stable,
language-neutral `code` columns that are all `NOT NULL` in the schema:

```text
AdministrativeState.code
AdministrativeDistrict.code
AdministrativeLocality.code
OrganizationUnitType.code
OrganizationUnit.code
Position.code
Shift.code
```

ORG-045 adopts `OrganizationCode` as their single normalization/validation policy.
All seven domain constructors now route code input through
`OrganizationCode.of(code).value()`, which rejects null/blank values, trims boundary
whitespace, and normalizes letters with `Locale.ROOT` upper case.

The public domain record components remain `String code` for these existing models.
Changing all seven accessor types to `OrganizationCode` would create broad persistence,
query, DTO, and compatibility churn without adding business value at this stage.
Instead, the active organization-unit write boundary adopts the value type directly:

```text
CreateOrganizationUnitRequest.code : String
        |
        v
OrganizationRestMapper
        |
        v
OrganizationCode
        |
        v
CreateOrganizationUnitCommand.code : OrganizationCode
        |
        v
OrganizationUnit.code : normalized String
```

A deprecated textual command constructor remains temporarily for internal compatibility.
API/OpenAPI request and response shapes remain textual and therefore do not change.

The value object is intentionally not applied to employee numbers, postal codes,
database IDs, topology resolver display codes, or polymorphic target IDs because those
belong to different identifier semantics.

No Flyway migration is added in ORG-045. Existing rows are not rewritten here; any
database-level canonical-code preflight or constraint can be considered together with
the ORG-046 integrity migration. Reads through the domain will normalize code values,
but the underlying historical stored value remains untouched until an explicit data
migration is approved.

Focused tests verify OrganizationCode normalization/rejection, all seven supported
model constructors, and typed adoption at the organization-unit creation command.

~~~~~~~~

**Pinned original bounded record — historical applicability:**

~~~~~~~~text
### ORG-046 implementation result

**Migration:** `V20260927_004__enforce_organization_internal_reference_integrity.sql`

ORG-046 adds database integrity only for references owned by the Organization module.
Before installing any constraint, one transactional preflight rejects direct orphan rows,
unsupported finite discriminators, and orphan polymorphic Organization targets.

Installed direct same-module foreign keys use `ON DELETE RESTRICT` for:

```text
AdministrativeDistrict.stateId -> AdministrativeState
AdministrativeLocality.districtId -> AdministrativeDistrict
EmployeeAddress.employeeId -> Employee
EmployeeAddress.localityId -> AdministrativeLocality
OrganizationUnit.unitTypeId -> OrganizationUnitType
OrganizationUnit.parentUnitId -> OrganizationUnit
EmployeeAssignment.employeeId -> Employee
EmployeeAssignment.organizationUnitId -> OrganizationUnit
EmployeeAssignment.positionId -> Position
ShiftAssignment.employeeId -> Employee
ShiftAssignment.shiftId -> Shift
ShiftAssignment.organizationUnitId -> OrganizationUnit
OrganizationDelegation.delegatorEmployeeId -> Employee
OrganizationDelegation.delegateEmployeeId -> Employee
OrganizationDelegation.responsibilityAssignmentId -> ResponsibilityAssignment
OrganizationHierarchySnapshot.capturedByEmployeeId -> Employee
```

Closed discriminator checks govern the polymorphic references already typed by earlier
Organization corrections:

```text
OrganizationContactPoint.targetType
  EMPLOYEE | ORGANIZATION_UNIT

ReportingLine.sourceType / targetType
  EMPLOYEE | POSITION | ORGANIZATION_UNIT

ResponsibilityAssignment.assigneeType
  EMPLOYEE | ORGANIZATION_UNIT
```

The migration also preflights target existence for those polymorphic references before
constraint installation. Their target IDs are intentionally not modeled with cross-table
or cross-module database foreign keys because one column can reference multiple
Organization tables and external ownership remains resolver-backed.

No topology, identity, pipeline, facility, equipment, or other bounded-context foreign
key is introduced. The existing canonical
`ResponsibilityAssignment.scopeId -> hidra_org_operational_scope.id` foreign key from
the operational-scope migration remains unchanged.

Focused PostgreSQL/Testcontainers tests prove direct FK/check installation, rejection of
invalid discriminator writes, and transaction rollback with source data preserved when
either a direct orphan or a polymorphic orphan is present.

~~~~~~~~

~~~~~~~~text
### ORG-047 implementation result

**Migration:** `V20260927_005__retire_organization_multilingual_compatibility_columns.sql`

ORG-047 retires exactly the three remaining language-ambiguous compatibility columns:

```text
hidra_org_unit_type.description
hidra_org_position.description
hidra_org_shift.name
```

The migration does not infer or translate any value. It fails transactionally before
the first DROP when a non-null legacy unit-type or position description is not already
preserved exactly in at least one corresponding embedded
`descriptionAr/descriptionFr/descriptionEn` field.

For Shift, retirement requires the legacy `name` to match the exact cutover projection
used by runtime compatibility writes: first nonblank English, then French, then Arabic,
then the stable code. Embedded names are boundary-trimmed for comparison because the
runtime compatibility projection trimmed the selected value.

The obsolete JPA mappings/accessors are removed from
`OrganizationUnitTypeJpaEntity`, `PositionJpaEntity`, and `ShiftJpaEntity`.
No domain, application, or REST multilingual contract changes are introduced.

Focused PostgreSQL/Testcontainers tests cover successful retirement and fail-closed
rollback for mismatched unit-type descriptions, position descriptions, and shift names.
The repository Boot smoke test already uses PostgreSQL/Testcontainers with
`spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate`, providing Hibernate validation against the
post-retirement schema in normal CI.

CI #380 initially failed during test compilation because the pre-existing multilingual
persistence mapper test still asserted the deliberately removed `ShiftJpaEntity.legacyName()`
compatibility accessor. The ORG-047 repair removes that obsolete assertion and renames the
test to describe post-retirement behavior; no production or migration semantics change.

~~~~~~~~

~~~~~~~~text
### ORG-048 implementation result

**Guardrail:** `OrganizationTypedDependencyIntegrityTest`

ORG-048 closes the typed-dependency correction sequence with repository-level tests only;
it does not change runtime behavior or schema.

The guardrail fixes the following invariants:

```text
Domain canonical polymorphic state
  OrganizationContactPoint.target -> ContactPointTargetReference
  ReportingLine.source/target -> ReportingSubjectReference
  ResponsibilityAssignment.assigneeType -> ResponsibilityAssigneeType

JPA canonical finite discriminators
  OrganizationContactPointJpaEntity.targetType -> ContactPointTargetType
  ReportingLineJpaEntity.sourceType/targetType -> ReportingSubjectType
  ResponsibilityAssignmentJpaEntity.assigneeType -> ResponsibilityAssigneeType
  all persisted with EnumType.STRING
```

Existing textual migration bridges are not deleted by this task because earlier roadmap
steps deliberately retained them for compatibility. ORG-048 instead requires every
wide textual constructor/accessor bridge in the governed models/entities to remain
explicitly `@Deprecated(forRemoval = true)`, preventing a raw-string compatibility path
from silently becoming canonical again.

Database guardrails assert that the ORG-046 same-module referential-integrity migration
continues to contain all 16 Organization-owned foreign keys and the four governed
polymorphic discriminator checks, together with its fail-closed preflight contract.

Multilingual guardrails assert that the ORG-047 JPA compatibility fields remain absent,
that the retirement migration still drops the three legacy columns, and that no later
migration restores those columns or the ORG-039 retired translation table.

Finally, every migration marked `Module: organization` is scanned for foreign keys to
non-`hidra_org_*` tables. This preserves the architecture rule that topology, identity,
and other bounded contexts are resolved through public contracts/stable references rather
than database ownership from Organization.

Normal CI provides the requested full compile/test/clean-verify gate for this final
guardrail task.

~~~~~~~~

#### Target contract and invariant ownership

Organization owns EmployeeAssignment membership and its lifecycle. One stable
assignment identity retains its original employee identity; transfer creates a
different assignment for that same employee, and correction records the exact
before/after image of the retained identity. Domain types compute/validate
immutable proposals; Application obtains current authorization, locks/versions,
applies the domain proposal and persists the full result in one transaction.
No actor name, expected version, policy object, request ID or domain proposal
is permission by itself. Ports expose immutable values, not JPA entities.

All effective intervals use [validFrom,validTo), with null validTo meaning an
explicitly open end. Adjacent intervals do not overlap. Interval overlap is
a.from<b.to AND b.from<a.to, treating absent ends as positive infinity.
Recorded time is independent from effective time and is server-derived at
runtime. No implicit scheduler, future status transition, employment termination,
Identity grant or operational responsibility change is invented.

END shortens an existing eligible interval without moving its start or changing
employee/unit/position/type; its endpoint must be after the start and must not
extend an already finite end. Preserve the original row/version in the journal.
A future endpoint is an end-date plan and does not mean the appointment has
already ended: keep ACTIVE until its effective boundary in current-as-of
evaluation; ENDED represents an already effective ending. Runtime backdating/
scheduling permissions and clock sampling require explicit later admission.

TRANSFER atomically closes the selected source at t and starts one new destination
assignment at t for the same employee, explicit unit/position/type/end and new ID.
t is strictly after the source start and before its existing finite end.
A transfer at an existing finite end is not a source-shortening transfer; use
an independently admitted adjacent creation instead. No gap/overlap at t;
destination reference/eligibility failure, conflict, authority loss or audit
failure rolls back both changes. No auto-closing of other assignments.

CORRECT retains assignment and employee IDs and createdAt, supplies an explicit
nonblank reason, and records the complete prior and proposed values. Unit,
position, type, interval or status correction is explicit, versioned and subject
to current authority and policy; never overwrite audit history or silently
rewrite another appointment. The domain can represent a correction, but its
presence does not authorize retroactive business effects. No hard DELETE is
part of the lifecycle.

A change value contains kind, exact versioned before image, exact after image,
optional transfer successor and reason. Its expected source version must be
positive and its resulting source version exactly +1, rejecting overflow.
The new transfer identity begins at version1. Proposed values are detached
immutable EmployeeAssignment records; no mutable collection/array or framework
type escapes. The before image must agree with the expected assignment identity
and version at the later persistence boundary.

#### Explicit concurrency and acting policy; no invented deployment default

There is no source-established organization-wide overlap rule. Package A will
provide an explicit immutable policy input with:
- a complete symmetric pair matrix for PRIMARY/SECONDARY/TEMPORARY/ACTING
  overlaps for one employee (including same-type diagonal);
- a positive maximum concurrent PRIMARY count for that employee;
- an explicit position-capacity mode: UNRESTRICTED or SINGLE_HOLDER, applied to
  the (organizationUnitId,positionId) pair, never to a shared position code alone.

All16 ordered matrix entries are required; asymmetry, unknown/missing type,
absent policy or invalid limits fail. There is no global constant selecting
the actual company's personnel policy, no HTTP-supplied override, and no
deployment permissiveness inferred from existing unconstrained inserts.
Synthetic tests must exercise both allowed and denied acting/secondary overlap
and both capacity modes. Passing a policy is a calculation input, not evidence
that a business owner approved it. Pair permission and PRIMARY count are
independent checks; both must allow a candidate. SINGLE_HOLDER forbids overlap
between different employees on the same unit/position pair, including ACTING;
a business need for simultaneous cover must select an explicit different policy
in a later admitted contract, not bypass the check by naming the type ACTING.

Only ACTIVE records contribute to concurrent occupancy in this first policy
contract. SUSPENDED/ENDED/CANCELLED remain historical data. Whether SUSPENDED
reserves a post is a future explicit policy revision, not silently assumed.
These are finite software-policy modes, not acceptance of an actual personnel
rule. Runtime policy selection/version/authority and effective activation remain
a required B prerequisite. Preserve four existing AssignmentType values.

Policy evaluation receives the proposed final relevant snapshot and validates
all overlaps/counts using effective-time intervals, not merely collection size.
Transfer validation replaces the source with its shortened image and adds the
successor before evaluation. Exact IDs must be unique; input collections are
copied. A caller-supplied incomplete snapshot cannot prove database concurrency.
Application/repository must later retrieve and lock the complete affected
employee and unit/position sets at the same transaction sample.

#### Required later runtime design, API and physical guarantees

One READ COMMITTED transaction must bind authenticated actor/current grants,
authoritative ownership/target eligibility, exact source versions, complete
affected overlap sets, policy revision, request receipt and journal commit.
Lock employee identities and all affected unit/position conflict keys in a
documented global order, then assignment rows in stable ID order; serialize
absence as well as existing rows. A nullable-row lock or application precheck
alone cannot prevent first-insert races. All creation aliases and maintenance
writers must obey the same protocol; constraint-valid direct SQL negatives
must be included in PostgreSQL proof. Row CAS uses a real persisted version;
no reliance on lastUpdated timestamps. Final admission must reject changed
authority/ownership; transaction/audit/commit failures never return success.
No automatic retry after an indeterminate physical commit.

Request idempotency is actor + authoritative resource scope + requestId, with a
canonical digest of typed command, expected versions and policy revision.
Identical replay requires fresh current authority and returns its original
immutable receipt, not a claim that the old result is current. Different input
under the same key conflicts. Store immutable before/after, optional successor,
effective/recorded time, native actor provenance, request/digest and policy
revision. Bind journal and source updates transactionally; database enforcement
must reject journal UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE including empty statements.
Fresh-schema tests use separate actual admin/runtime principals. Do not assume
the current JPA save path provides these guarantees.

Proposed lifecycle transport, not existing endpoints: POST /assignments/{id}/end,
POST /assignments/{id}/transfer, POST /assignments/{id}/corrections under
/api/v1/organization; scoped GET history by assignment, employee and unit/position.
Commands require explicit requestId, expectedVersion, typed effective fields,
reason and destination where applicable; reject actor/grants/policy claims and
unknown/coerced fields. Preserve existing create aliases and read shapes until
their explicit cutover/compatibility review. New reads use database-bounded
keyset pagination with limit1..100, stable (recordedTime,eventId) ordering and
a scope/filter-bound captured high-water boundary. Cursor values are untrusted
query data, never authority. Exact historical version lookup is independent
of page size and current projection. History preserves versions after transfer
or correction without disclosing foreign employee/unit/position metadata.
400 invalid transport,401 unauthenticated, non-disclosing403/404 by registered
scope policy,409 CAS/replay/policy conflict and safe503 unavailable/indeterminate.
No public route is registered by this design.

**Concrete runtime blockers:** the reviewed owner records provide no authoritative
company binding and no reviewed employee-appointment scoped authorization export.
A hierarchy root or arbitrary company field cannot supply that authority.
Before B, source-review genuine Identity and Organization/Party ownership contracts,
decide whether admission is exact unit/employee-resource scoped or requires a
separate company-ownership relation, register exact public exported types and
temporal/concurrency proof. Do not use a public permission set/Boolean, stale
JWT grant, generic Platform exception or foreign concrete adapter. Broader
ownership changes require explicit bounded registration, not hidden scope growth.
The current assignment create bypass and existing broad listing also need exact
compatibility/writer remediation paths in B. These requirements do not block
pure Package A or require industrial calibration values.

**Implemented bounded source:**
EmployeeAppointmentChange is an immutable detached proposal with END/TRANSFER/
CORRECT kind, exact versioned before/after, optional transfer successor, explicit
reason and recorded-time input. It preserves assignment/employee identity and
creation time for changes, requires strict +1 version with overflow rejection,
and binds updatedAt to recordedAt with backward-observation rejection.
END cannot extend a finite interval or change membership/start; future endings
stay ACTIVE and already effective endings are ENDED. TRANSFER shortens an
ACTIVE source and starts a distinct version1 identity for the same employee at
the exact end boundary. Finite successor intervals are validated by the existing
EmployeeAssignment constructor; failed construction never changes source values.
A completed successor interval is represented ENDED instead of falsely ACTIVE.
CORRECT retains complete prior/proposed images, stable assignment/employee/
createdAt and an explicit reason; no transfer successor is allowed. No system
clock, permission, native actor assertion, receipt, persistence or scheduler is
implemented. Recorded time supplied to a pure function is not trusted authority.

EmployeeAppointmentPolicy copies a complete symmetric sixteen-entry type-pair
matrix, requires a positive PRIMARY limit and explicit UNRESTRICTED/SINGLE_HOLDER
mode, and selects no actual personnel policy. It rejects missing/asymmetric/
null matrices and invalid limits. It validates all ACTIVE final-snapshot
overlaps and coalesces timestamp deltas per employee to count effective concurrent
PRIMARY appointments using half-open boundaries, including unbounded ends.
SINGLE_HOLDER applies to different employees sharing the same unit/position
pair, including ACTING; different units/positions remain separate. Non-ACTIVE
records remain in returned history but do not contribute occupancy under this
explicitly registered first software-policy mode.

Policy.apply requires the exact observed before image and version, replaces
the source and adds the successor before validation, rejects duplicate IDs,
and returns an immutable copy. On any failure the observed input remains
untouched. Both proposed scopes and complete conflict discovery must still be
secured and locked by a future runtime owner; no caller-supplied list, matrix
or valid domain record is a persistence/concurrency/authority proof.
All production imports are Java or existing Organization domain types only.
Existing EmployeeAssignment, AssignmentType, AssignmentStatus, controllers,
services, repositories, SQL/migrations and responsibility behavior are unchanged.

#### Concrete ownership choice before B implementation

The existing data cannot distinguish the following two business contracts.
They must not be collapsed into an inferred company model:

**Option A — recommended, explicit company ownership for units.** Introduce an
Organization-owned immutable company/unit binding with a neutral Party reference
and authoritative eligibility through an Organization-specific Party export.
Bind each appointment to its unit's exact binding revision; preserve historical
binding/assignment linkage. No inherited hierarchy ownership and no silent
rebind on parent changes. Initial scope permits transfers only within the same
bound company; cross-company employment transfer is outside this package and
requires a separate approved contract. Employee identity remains Organization-
owned and reusable; its personal/history access still requires employee-specific
authority. Binding a unit to a company does not assert that every employee
record globally belongs to that company or that every ACTIVE Party is a legally
qualified employer. Party eligibility semantics must be explicit in registration.

**Option B — narrower, exact unit/employee authorization without company ownership.**
Use genuine ORGANIZATION_UNIT grants plus an explicit employee-resource scope
and current source/destination resource authority. No company field, Party
binding or company-isolation claim is introduced. Two isolated grant domains
can be tested, but this cannot satisfy a later requirement for authoritative
company ownership or reporting; that requirement remains unmet, not waived.

This review recommends A to retain company/resource governance, but does not
record the owner's selection. A materially changes ownership semantics/schema
and the permitted transfer boundary; B deliberately narrows the company claim.
An explicit choice is required before either conditional runtime envelope below
becomes executable. The currently registered pure domain Package A and its
configurable policy semantics remain valid under either choice.

#### Conditional protected authorization and policy activation contract

For either option, proposed exact action family is CREATE, END, TRANSFER,
CORRECT, READ_CURRENT, READ_HISTORY and READ_POLICY, with explicit permission
definitions and no role/user grants. Permission/resource codes and qualified
native request serialization must be fixed in the next admission record,
not derived from a caller string. Requests carry explicit identifiers/action,
never user ID, claims, grants, policy objects or authority scalars.
Current native authentication is prepared outside the transaction and consumed
once by the genuine Identity owner on the same physical connection as the
appointment operation. Company/unit/employee/resource decisions, where applicable,
use one authoritative sample and validity interval. Any DENY wins; missing or
indeterminate evidence fails closed. Fresh request authorization is required on
idempotent replay and exact historical reads. A read-only policy query is not
policy activation authority.

Option A additionally requires company-scoped and exact source/destination unit
decisions, employee-history/identity access, current binding revision and Party
eligibility. Option B requires exact source/destination unit and employee
decisions, without calling an arbitrary requested company ID authoritative.
No protected assignment lookup, foreign count, existence, history or policy
payload is disclosed before the relevant current authority is established.

Deployment policy selection is not inferred from enum names or request bodies.
Persist versioned explicit matrices/PRIMARY limits/capacity mode with provenance;
a lifecycle command uses the exact active policy revision or fails closed.
Read access cannot edit policy, bootstrap activates no permissive default, and
synthetic fixtures may explicitly supply policies. SUSPENDED occupancy remains
the finite domain rule documented in A until a separately approved policy
revision changes it. This is not approval of an actual personnel regulation.

Required physical order: acquire genuine Identity fences and, for A, Party
eligibility and binding fences; freeze descriptor requirements; authorize;
resolve exact source/reference/policy state; lock all affected employee and
unit/position conflict keys in stable order including absent-key serialization;
apply domain proposal; finite source/journal/receipt writes; managed flush;
one final time/native/owner/policy/version/lock guard; observed physical commit.
One transaction must roll back source close, successor creation, receipt and
journal together. Any technical executor extension needs exact new compiled

No exact lock census, private credential path or final SQL is invented by this

#### Closed ownership and eligibility contract

Organization owns an immutable binding identified by binding ID, positive
revision, organization-unit ID, neutral company Party ID and recordedAt.
All identifiers are nonblank normalized strings; recordedAt is explicit.
A revision is an immutable fact, not an editable row. A separate current pointer
may later advance monotonically under protected administrative authority.
A unit has at most one current binding. No hierarchy traversal, reparenting,
position label or employee record supplies an implicit binding.

Every protected appointment snapshot pins its exact binding ID and revision.
The pin must match the snapshot's exact unit. Historical pins never resolve
through a current pointer and are not rewritten on pointer changes. A source
snapshot carries its original pin; newly created or moved destination snapshots
require the current destination binding. Ending preserves the source pin.
Correction preserves assignment/employee identity and historical before-image;
a correction moving unit requires both source and destination authority and
a new destination pin. Every before/after/successor company in one change must
match exactly. Cross-company transfer or correction is rejected, not split into
an apparent same-company operation. No automatic change to Employee,
ResponsibilityAssignment, Workflow decisions or Identity grants is permitted.

Party eligibility means only that the referenced Party currently exists and is
ACTIVE/selectable for a new technical Organization reference. It does not certify
an employer, labor-law status or employee ownership. The Organization-specific
Party export must say so and issue genuine transaction-bound eligibility
evidence; no direct foreign JPA read or Topology ticket reuse is allowed.
ACTIVE is necessary at new binding/appointment admission, with current eligibility
rechecked at the final protected guard. Revocation denies new protected writes.
Historical retention does not depend on continued ACTIVE status; an authorized
history read can show its immutable pin without treating it as current eligibility.
A binding change freezes new admissions to the old revision, not history.
Existing unbound rows remain retained legacy data: no inferred backfill, no
manufactured Party, no operational activation until explicitly bound and migrated.

#### Fixed authority vocabulary and policy boundary

Reserve exact permissions organization.appointment.create, .end, .transfer,
.correct, .read-current, .read-history and .read-policy (each suffix expands
after organization.appointment). No grant/role bootstrap is authorized.
Native requests carry action, identifiers, expected versions and idempotency
key only; no caller-supplied identity, claims, policy, sample or credentials.

The company resource is ORGANIZATION_COMPANY with CUSTOM scope and exact
Party ID; employee resource ORGANIZATION_EMPLOYEE with CUSTOM scope and
exact employee ID; unit resource ORGANIZATION_UNIT with ORGANIZATION_UNIT
scope and exact unit ID. Resource ID and scope reference must agree exactly.
These are explicit resource namespaces, not new ScopeType enum values.
The fixed action permission must be decided for every required company,
employee and source/destination unit at one native sample. Assignment ID
is a protected selector, never an alternative scope or bearer capability.
READ_POLICY needs company/unit decisions, not unrelated employee data.
Employee-specific reads additionally require the exact employee decision;
unit/position occupancy pages need the company/unit decisions and must omit
personal details without corresponding employee authority. History of a move
requires all companies/units represented by the returned versions; no foreign
count, existence, journal payload or pagination metadata leaks before admission.
Missing scope must be rejected before AuthorizationScope's GLOBAL default.
No administrative bypass or protected executor wildcard is reserved here.

Actual Identity support must add a private Organization native family,
opaque issuer-owned preparation/admission, qualified one-use claim evidence
and exact dispatcher registration, not an EvaluatePermissionQuery Boolean.
Policy activation is an independently protected explicit versioned configuration
operation: immutable matrix, PRIMARY limit, capacity mode, actor/provenance and
active pointer. No permissive default, client policy or implicit bootstrap.
The existing pure EmployeeAppointmentPolicy remains the invariant evaluator;
a domain value supplied to B1 is not proof of active policy or authority.

#### B2 native and owner protocol to implement

The Identity request has the fixed action, exact bounded company/unit descriptors
and an employee selector when required. Descriptors are immutable scalar request
data, never ownership evidence. Missing identifiers/scope, unsupported combinations,
duplicates or noncanonical ordering fail before authority consumption.

CREATE/END require one pair; TRANSFER/CORRECT one or two pairs in one company.
READ_POLICY carries no employee; mutation requests require one exact employee.
READ_CURRENT/READ_HISTORY support a unit/position view without employee details
or an employee-specific view requiring the employee decision. History spanning
companies must include every represented company and unit in the same group;
a caller cannot omit a foreign historical pin and still receive that row/count.
These limits bound technical evaluation, not deployed personnel policy.

into one private Organization claim group, all action-specific resource requests
using the same contribution/sample, native binding/session/user, validUntil,
thread, current Authentication object, physical connection, backend PID and XID.

with exact unit ID. Resource reference equals scope reference. Fixed resource
kind determines the permission code. The contract accepts no arbitrary code,
claims, user ID, Boolean authorization result or public credential factory.
One-use private child credentials and an owner-family discriminator must prevent
station/draft/publication/diagnostic credentials crossing into Organization.
No resource prefix escape or engineeringDraft=true shortcut is acceptable.

The qualified reader loads every graph under existing native/Identity fences,
then the real AuthorizationPolicyEvaluator evaluates every decision at the
single sample. Any DENY wins; missing/indeterminate fails closed. Expiry is
bounded by all relevant native/evidence limits. Opaque Prepared/Admission tickets

rollback-only state, completed transaction and replay; all failure paths poison

scalar authority with the genuine owner. Constructible contributions and fence
lists never become credentials. Preserve current station/draft/publication
permission sets and all existing diagnostics' non-authority behavior.

- hidra_org_appointment_lock_key: permanent typed unique

  employee; OCCUPANCY uses exact unit/position; REQUEST uses native actor user,

- hidra_org_appointment_event: immutable UUID event, operation, source/successor,

  reason, command digest, native binding/session/user, sample/validUntil, PID/XID.
  The canonical payload contains the exact typed command and every full snapshot;

  CREATE has no before and version1 after; END/CORRECT have exactly one +1 source;
  TRANSFER has exactly one +1 source and one distinct version1 successor. A deferred
  completeness check rejects missing/extra rows for that event.
  Full pinned binding facts accompany every snapshot. Event order uses
  (sampled_at,event_id); do not use mutable assignment timestamps as versions.
- hidra_org_appointment_receipt: immutable event link, native actor, exact scope
  digest/requestId and command digest, full immutable result, commit-guard time
  and PID/XID. Unique (actor_user_id,scope_key,request_id), event uniqueness and
  deferred source/event/receipt consistency; a receipt is historical, not current
  permission. No automatic retry after an indeterminate commit.

#### One universal lock, authorization and finalization protocol

All application writers and both config procedures use this class order, NOWAIT
for owner relation fences and bounded transaction/statement timeouts. A conflict
fails safely; it never increases the executor's500ms aggregate budget:

1. Genuine Identity/native24 relation fences in their existing fixed order.
   Database-only config procedures take the same exact relation-lock order under
   their distinct administrative ACL; they do not mint native Identity tickets
   or claim an application-user PERMIT. Application writes use the genuine export.
2. Party's2 existing owner fences in their existing fixed order for writes/new
   references; authorized historical retention does not require current ACTIVE.
3. Organization relation fences in this fixed order: employee, organization_unit,
   position, binding_revision, binding_head, policy_revision, policy_head,
   configuration_event, lock_key, employee_assignment, appointment_event,
   appointment_receipt (all exact public.hidra_org_ names; the full names are
   defined above/below). The exact12 are public.hidra_org_employee,
   public.hidra_org_organization_unit, public.hidra_org_position,
   public.hidra_org_appointment_binding_revision,
   public.hidra_org_appointment_binding_head,
   public.hidra_org_appointment_policy_revision,
   public.hidra_org_appointment_policy_head,
   public.hidra_org_appointment_configuration_event,
   public.hidra_org_appointment_lock_key, public.hidra_org_employee_assignment,
   public.hidra_org_appointment_event, public.hidra_org_appointment_receipt.
   Use SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE for mutable owner relations,
   ACCESS SHARE for immutable revisions/events while observing; config writers
   take the corresponding mutually conflicting owner fences before head changes.
   Never take a row/key lock then request an earlier owner fence. The conservative
   assignment relation fence serializes first-key creation before any privileged
   INSERT, including empty tables; concurrency optimization requires later proof.
4. A bounded internal SELECT-only descriptor preview may precede owner locks
   solely to construct B2's exact request (including the old alias's server-derived
   company/unit selectors). It never returns data or authority and takes no row/
   explicit owner lock; no mutable decision relies on that preview. Acquire the
   Identity fences first using those selector values, then Party/Organization in
   the order above. Re-read under retained owner fences and require exact closure
   equality, or reject uniformly. This avoids taking an Organization owner fence
   before the native owner merely to discover the request's descriptors.
   Freeze current/pinned descriptor closure and active policy revisions privately.
   Acquire actual native admission for the fixed action and all exact descriptors;
   evaluate every required resource at one native sample before payload/counts.
   Internal bounded discovery is not permission or a disclosed result. Limit101
   proves overflow of the100-descriptor technical bound and fails uniformly.
   Caller descriptors/cursors are selectors only; require exact complete equality
   with discovered source/destination/returned-history pins before disclosure.
5. Under retained relation fences resolve the exact source before version,
   current destination binding/policy and complete conflict observations. END and
   same-unit CORRECT retain the source pin; moved CORRECT/TRANSFER require the
   current destination pin; all before/after/successor companies agree. Reject
   cross-company mutation and never rewrite historical pins on rebind. Validate
   employee/unit/position eligibility, pure domain/ownership policy and overflow.
   Conflict discovery loads the source plus all ACTIVE rows for the affected
   employee or either unit/position, with a combined1025-row overflow probe and
   admitted1024-row bound. No omitted peer can prove completeness.
   Check an admitted existing receipt before demanding CAS against the current
   projection: an identical original typed command/digest may return its historical
   result after fresh native authorization for every recorded result descriptor;
   changed input, versions or policy under the same key conflicts without payload.
   A new request must satisfy current CAS. No replay turns an old version into
   mutation authority. Finish all owner/evidence queries and pure proposal work
   before opening the provisional phase; freeze the exact key/row/result set.
6. Seal admission once, obtain only the exact compiled coordinator's one-use
   permit, and open one provisional block admitting only the six fixed templates.
   Insert then lock EMPLOYEE keys sorted by ID; insert then lock OCCUPANCY keys
   sorted (unit,position); lock source assignment rows sorted by ID; then insert
   and lock REQUEST keys sorted (actor,scope,requestId). KEY_INS/KEY_LOCK/SOURCE_LOCK
   must return the exact expected key/row version. The earlier relation fences
   serialize absence and retain the entire observed conflict/source set until
   these locks exist. Config procedures use the same order for affected keys.
   Persist source close/correction or creation, optional transfer successor and
   exactly one event using only ASSIGNMENT_INS/ASSIGNMENT_CAS/EVENT_INS. CAS must
   affect exactly1. No owner callback, arbitrary SQL, new evidence query or ORM
   flush runs inside PROVISIONAL; the two exact lock SELECTs use executeQuery.
   A replay performs no new mutation/key/event and follows the read final guard.
7. Close the provisional block once, then recheck owner admission outside that
   phase and materialize detached results. Both transfer rows/event stay in the
   same physical transaction; receipt/audit/guard failures roll back all changes.
   A swallowed SQL/owner failure poisons the transaction rather than allowing a
   second provisional block or an alternate write path.
8. In FLUSHING, flush any managed work, recheck actual Identity and Party tickets,
   all current/pinned heads/revisions, policy, retained locks, role/catalog, full
   final evidence graphs and version/event consistency. After this, GUARD issues
   exactly ONE scalar statement: actual database time within [sample,validUntil),
   same physical PID/XID and exact owner lock/state proof; write guard creates the
   immutable receipt only if every condition holds. Read guard is non-mutating.
   No owner query, ORM lazy load, refresh or serialization SQL follows GUARD.
   SQL-free beforeCommit invalidation veto and observed physical commit remain
   required. Swallowed failure, rollback-only, suspension or unknown commit never
   returns a successful result; INDETERMINATE has safe reconciliation semantics.

#### Routes, strict values and non-disclosing reads

New controller mappings under /api/v1/organization (method names after semicolons):

- POST /assignments/{id}/end; end
- POST /assignments/{id}/transfer; transfer
- POST /assignments/{id}/corrections; correct
- GET /assignments/{id}/history; assignmentHistory
- GET /assignments/{id}/versions/{version}; exactVersion
- GET /employees/{employeeId}/appointment-history; employeeHistory
- GET /units/{unitId}/positions/{positionId}/appointment-history; positionHistory

companies, oversized payload/cursor, nonpositive intervals and unsupported
precision before mutation. Timestamp canonicalization must round-trip exactly at
PostgreSQL microsecond precision; never silently lose nanoseconds in CAS/digests.

boundary and cursor bound to selector/filter/order. Validate cursor syntax/bounds
but do not trust its scope. Obtain and authorize the complete descriptor closure
for the selected historical rows before returning even count/cursor metadata;
foreign versions outside a page cannot be hidden to claim the selected assignment
has only authorized history. Employee-specific pages require employee authority;
unit/position pages without it return occupancy identity/version/interval/pin
only, omitting employee ID/name and personal fields. Exact version lookup has its
own current authorization and never depends on a page having included the row.
Party retirement does not erase authorized immutable history. Policy read requires
only the actual company/unit READ_POLICY decisions and never activates policy.

Return400 for invalid transport,401 unauthenticated, uniform403 for unavailable
or unauthorized protected selectors regardless of existence,409 for admitted
version/policy/overlap/replay conflicts, and safe503 for unavailable/indeterminate
execution. Only after complete authorization may an absent exact version yield404.

historical and subject to fresh current authorization; no stale PERMIT is cached.

#### Native issuer and proof transport

Extend the existing approved Organization Identity contract, not another generic
signer/export. Add CommitIntent(eventId UUID, commandSha256, payloadSha256,
operationValidUntil), CommitProof(frame bytes, MAC bytes) and the two methods:
`issueCommitProof(Admission, CommitIntent)` and
`commitProofFences(Admission)`. Intent digests must be exact lowercase32-byte
SHA256 encodings and eventId nonnull; expiry must be exact PostgreSQL
microseconds, after the original sample and no later than native validUntil.
Intent contains no actor, session, user, PID, XID, permission, key, audience or
caller-selected authorized scope. Proof byte arrays are defensively copied,
strictly bounded and redacted by toString; constructing this transport is not
authority. Do not return it in REST, JWT, audit text, diagnostics or normal logs.

Only the actual participant's private, completed and still-current mutating
Admission can issue. Reuse its exact Request, complete PERMIT graph, genuine
native actor/binding/session, original sample/deadline and physical coordinates.
Recheck original Authentication object, thread, transaction, holder, native
origin and graph through the existing owners. Refuse read actions, fabricated/
foreign/replayed/suspended/completed admissions, unavailable or non-PERMIT
evidence and any attempted broader/longer intent. One issuer use per Admission;
a fresh application replay obtains fresh native authority but creates no new
lifecycle receipt and cannot reuse an old commit proof. No public sign(bytes),
caller-built credential, scalar actor header or GUC can reach the signing key.
Full process compromise and trusted database/key administrators remain explicit
trust boundaries; no cryptographic non-repudiation or immunity to them is claimed.

#### Authenticated encoding and independent key material

Use HMAC-SHA256, described accurately as a keyed message-authentication proof,
not an asymmetric digital signature. Java uses the standard JCA implementation;
PostgreSQL verification uses pgcrypto hmac(bytea,bytea,text), never a plain hash,
home-grown HMAC, JWT-secret reuse or a database function that signs arbitrary
input. Official PostgreSQL16
[pgcrypto documentation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/pgcrypto.html)
supports this API and records its OpenSSL dependency. None of the164 exact
current migration sources references pgcrypto:161 were recovered locally and
matched by Git blob hash, the remaining3 were retrieved by their live blob SHA.
This is source/dependency inspection, not extension availability proof.

The additive migration may install pgcrypto in a fixed migration-owned
`hidra_identity_crypto` namespace. Verify actual installed namespace/owner/
function identity and dependency availability in PostgreSQL16 CI. Do not move
an existing extension, grant schema CREATE to an application role, install
unreviewed crypto software at runtime or silently accept an unsafe pre-existing
placement. A bad catalog fails closed. No POM or workflow change is admitted.

New configuration prefix: `hidra.identity.organization-commit-proof`, with
enabled=false, key-id, positive key-revision and signing-key-base64. Disabled
configuration loads no key and preserves existing authentication/read behavior;
calling proof issuance while disabled rejects. Enabled configuration requires
an explicitly supplied32-byte random key, exact key identity/revision and safe
encoding. There is no repository/development key default. Use external secret
binding and test-only synthetic material; redact every accessor representation,
bind value, exception and diagnostic. This approval does not change JWT rotation,
select a production secret manager or authorize production-secret handling.

The wire frame is versioned, unambiguous and deterministic. Freeze the exact
Java/SQL byte vectors in the implementation tests: UTF-8 domain
`HIDRA/IDENTITY/ORG-APPOINTMENT-COMMIT/1`, protocol version, database audience UUID,
observed publisher session login, key ID/revision, issuer-generated32-byte nonce,
native binding/session UUIDs, actor user ID, fixed action, complete canonical
company/unit vector and employee, native sample/deadline, narrowed operation
deadline, PID/XID, event UUID, command SHA256 and canonical full-envelope SHA256.
Text/vector fields use explicit big-endian lengths/counts; UUIDs and digests have
fixed binary widths. Timestamps are signed64-bit epoch microseconds without
rounding; reject non-exact/overflowed values. Mutation vectors contain at most
two distinct pairs, retain the existing Java String ordering and reject duplicate
or incomplete pairs. The SQL codec must reproduce UTF-16 ordering for supplementary
Unicode as well as BMP identifiers; locale/collation defaults may not change it.
Bound the whole frame to4096 bytes and MAC to32. MAC comparison must inspect all
32 bytes without an early mismatch return.

The participant derives these authority/context fields from its private ticket
and retained database key context, not CommitIntent. SQL derives the expected
command/payload hashes and resource scope from the real event and complete pinned
before/after/successor snapshots. It must reject a valid MAC for another action,
scope, actor, database, publisher, event, result, key generation or transaction.
The original native deadline is signed and cannot be extended by Organization.

#### Identity-owned verifier storage, provisioning and lock order

The migration owns exactly three new logical Identity relations:

- `public.hidra_identity_org_commit_key_event`: immutable administrative key
  activation/revocation metadata and monotonic revision history; fingerprint,
  audience, publisher and administrator provenance only, never a retained raw key.
- `public.hidra_identity_org_commit_key_head`: current key ID/revision, audience,
  explicitly allowed publisher login, active/revoked state and private current key
  bytes. Restricted activation replaces the old secret; old secret material must
  not be copied into immutable history. No delete/reset/ABA or default key.
- `public.hidra_identity_org_commit_proof_use`: immutable consumed key/revision/
  nonce and transaction/event/digest provenance, unique one-use key. No raw proof,
  raw key or unrelated claims. Event UUID is an opaque cross-owner reference,
  not a foreign aggregate or cross-module ownership transfer.

No ordinary, publisher or Organization configuration role gets key-table
SELECT/DML, key activation, crypto namespace ownership or a signing API.
Key activation/revocation is an explicit Identity-owned SECURITY DEFINER
administrative routine with a fixed safe path and PUBLIC EXECUTE revoked;
the environment administrator explicitly grants it to a distinct non-elevated
Identity key administrator. Migration creates no login/password, grant or active
key. Use session_user provenance, expected-revision CAS, immutable metadata and
restricted role/catalog checks. Key revision changes/revocation atomically reject
subsequent old proofs, with no implicit dual-key grace or production rotation
cadence inferred. Runtime and DB key mismatch always rejects. Document the actual
development provisioning/retirement contract in the admitted secrets document;
never put a real secret or secret-bearing SQL invocation in repository examples.

For proof-enabled write actions, after the existing native24 Identity fences and
BEFORE Party/Organization fences, acquire these additional Identity relation
fences in order: key_event ACCESS SHARE, key_head SHARE,
proof_use SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE, all NOWAIT. A tightly scoped metadata routine may
return only key identity/revision, audience, allowed publisher and retained
physical coordinates to the actual key adapter; it returns neither key bytes
nor a MAC and authenticates the actual session login/catalog/transaction.
The native participant retains its opaque key context in its own private Ticket.
Do not acquire an earlier Identity/key fence late during FLUSHING or GUARD.
Key administration observes the corresponding order and never requests an earlier
owner fence after a later one. Initial writes use explicit fixture provisioning.

Preserve the existing Identity finalFences24 contract for old clients/families;
the new commitProofFences exports only these3 additional already-held requirements.
The Organization writer's final complete union is therefore41 distinct relations:
Identity24 + proof3 + Party2 + Organization12. Existing station/draft/publication
counts and global fence helpers remain unchanged. Recheck catalog settings,
physical holder/PID/XID/session user, key generation and issuer evidence before

SQL verification/nonce consumption is a private Identity-owned SECURITY DEFINER
routine, fixed safe path, PUBLIC EXECUTE revoked. Its EXECUTE remains unavailable
to ordinary/publisher/Organization-config clients; the trusted Organization final
guard's function owner can invoke it internally. It verifies the authenticated

generation/audience/publisher and actual database time/PID/XID. It discloses no

ordinary application caller.

Nonce consumption and actual appointment receipt insertion must be in the same

rejects; rollback removes consumption and every provisional key/source/successor/
